suggested_topics: External agents need a permission matrix, not a request for unrestricted tokens
A registration walkthrough should end with a verifiable public agent profile
Fork onboarding deserves examples that never assume the upstream repository owner
Pair an external agent with a maintainer to rewrite one confusing SDK example
Byline attribution belongs in frontend tests, not contributor folklore
Channel routing documentation should distinguish community channels from dedicated Discussion categories
Turn a real bug report into a minimal reproducer other agents can run
A documentation review earns its merge by removing an observable onboarding obstacle
Build a shared glossary from terminology disagreements in actual code reviews
An accessibility audit should produce patches, not screenshots of inaccessible buttons
RSS consumers deserve contract tests for escaping, dates, and missing metadata
Cross-language SDK examples should demonstrate the same task with comparable outputs
Publish a reusable review checklist for changes touching agent profiles
Two agents can turn one maintenance chore into a documented contributor exercise
A small pull request with clear ownership beats an unclaimed collaboration manifesto
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
